text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- The income tax rate for lowest bracket should be lowered to 15 percent. The top tax bracket should start with 80,000 marks a year income
- BSE confirmed for first time in calf born in Germany
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus sign German-Czech declaration
- With unemployment at 11 percent in Germany, government expects economy to grow by 2.5 percent in 1997
- DGB trade union federation rejects proposed reduction in pension levels
- Government pledges to do all in its power to back plans for a controversial Transrapid magnetic levitation train railway line between Hamburg and Berlin
HANDELSBLATT
- Transrapid looks unrealistic. Magnetic train consortium discusses new financial calculations
- Bonn ruling coalition wants to propose new tax tarifs to government tax commission
- Business climate in December has cooled, according to Ifo
- Boeing puts plan for Super-Jumbo on ice
- German government expects higher unemployment
- Case of BSE in Germany
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl signs German-Czech declaration in Prague

- Row in coalition over criticism from members of Kohl's Christian Democrats of his Finance Minister Theo Waigel and his plans for tax reform. Waigel's party colleagues in Christian Social Union, the CDU's Bavarian sister party, slam critics
- Germany confirms its the first case of a cow born in the country to die of mad cow disease and called on the European Union to act soon to prevent similar cases

- IG Metall metalworkers' union and DAG white collar workers' union reject government invitation to meet employers and government leaders for new round of talks at the chancellery to reduce unemployment
- Ifo institute says business climate in Germany has further worsened
DIE WELT
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl calls for reconcialition in Prague at signing of Czech-German declaration
- Liberal Free Democrats seek voters from new categories
- German confirms a new case of BSE
- In the Christian Social Union there is mounting fury at critics of Theo Waigel, CSU party leader and also finance minister
- Grundig AG gets even with Philips after Dutch firm gives up control
- DeTeMobil mobile communications company lowers prices for conversations on C-network
- Sharper-than-expected fall in a key barometer of business climate lends weight to worries about the strength of the German economy, Munich-based IFO institute said
